Zvi Zwilling, son of Hana and Netanel, was born on 1 Adar II 5673 (10 March 1913) in Pinsk, Russia. In 1926 he immigrated with his family to Eretz Israel. The family settled in Tel Aviv, and Zvi studied at the Herzliya Gymnasium. After completing his studies he went to France to further his training in medicine. Before he turned twenty-four he was certified as a Doctor of Medicine by the faculty in Strasbourg. His doctoral thesis received much praise and was published in professional medical literature around the world. He turned down attractive job offers and preferred to return to the country. At first he worked at Hadassah Hospital, and afterwards he joined the Medical Association. His fellow doctors and the patients he treated held him in great esteem. He always kept his composure and his good spirits. He often refused to accept payment for treatment, and he would even pay his patients' medical expenses out of his own pocket.

Shortly after the outbreak of the Second World War he volunteered for the British Army, despite his parents' opposition. He served in Sudan and Ethiopia under difficult field conditions, and earned great respect there. Emperor Haile Selassie came in person to visit him and express his appreciation. Throughout his service he maintained a steady correspondence with his parents and showed concern for their welfare. In 1945 he returned to the country and worked at the military hospital in Haifa. Shortly before his discharge, on 28 Av 5705 (7 August 1945), he was killed in a road accident. He was laid to rest in the Nahalat Yitzhak Cemetery and is survived by his parents. His name is commemorated in the "Book of Volunteers," and the auditorium of the Tel Aviv doctors' building is named after him.

Further details of his service in the British Army: Dr. Zvi Zwilling (Zwilling Zvi), personal number 183869. He enlisted in the British Army and was posted to the Royal Army Medical Corps (R.A.M.C.). His rank in the British Army was Captain (Dr.). He was laid to rest in the TEL AVIV (NAHLAT YITZHAK) CEMETERY, Israel. Grave location: Plot 15, Row 12, Grave 24.
